# Photosynthesis

Photosynthesis is the process plants use to turn light energy into chemical energy stored in sugar.

## Light reactions

The light reactions happen in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast. Chlorophyll absorbs light and splits water molecules. This releases oxygen as a by-product and produces ATP and NADPH.

## Calvin cycle

The Calvin cycle takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast. It uses ATP and NADPH from the light reactions to fix carbon dioxide into sugar. The enzyme RuBisCO captures carbon dioxide in the first step of the cycle.

## Why it matters

Photosynthesis produces most of the oxygen in the atmosphere. Almost every food chain on Earth starts with organisms that perform photosynthesis. Scientists estimate that photosynthesis captures about 130 terawatts of energy worldwide.
